chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Abu al-Mughira', from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah, Most Majestic, Most Glorious, has placed both parents alongside all other heirs who have ordained shares, and has not reduced their share below one-sixth for each of them. And He has placed the husband and wife alongside all other heirs, and has not reduced their share below one-fourth and one-eighth.

key_terms.الأَبَوَانِ: both parents — the father and mother collectively, each protected at one-sixth
key_terms.الثُّمُنُ: one-eighth (thumn) — the minimum share of the wife when the deceased has children
key_terms.الرُّبُعُ: one-fourth (rub') — the minimum share of the husband when the deceased has no children
key_terms.السُّدُسُ: one-sixth (sudus) — the minimum share guaranteed to each parent in inheritance
key_terms.الْفَرَائِضُ: ordained shares — the fixed portions of inheritance prescribed by Quranic law (fara'id)
key_terms.الْمَوَارِيثُ: inheritances (mawaris) — the system of Islamic estate distribution
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Most Majestic, Most Glorious — an honorific for God emphasizing His greatness

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum guaranteed inheritance share for parents and spouses in Islamic law according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes a fundamental principle of Islamic inheritance law: that parents and spouses hold protected minimum shares that cannot be reduced regardless of the number of other heirs present. The parents are each guaranteed a minimum of one-sixth (sudus) of the estate, and the spouse receives a minimum of one-fourth (for a husband with no children) or one-eighth (for a wife with children). This ruling reflects the Quranic inheritance verses (4:11-12) and addresses the legal mechanism of 'awl (proportional reduction) in cases where the total prescribed shares exceed the estate.
